name: Severe Early-Onset Axonal Neuropathy Due to MFN2 Deficiency
aliases: Severe Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2A (CMT2A) Early-Onset Form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: MFN2-Related Early-Onset Axonal Neuropathy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset (infancy to early childhood) of progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potentials and preserved conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic biallelic or dominant mutations in the MFN2 gene
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance of neuropathy
Muscle biopsy showing neurogenic atrophy and mitochondrial abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset progressive distal axonal neuropathy with electrophysiological confirmation and pathogenic MFN2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; electrophysiological studies support clinical findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Severe sensory loss in distal extremities
searchTerms: severe numbness in hands and feet
major sensory loss in distal extremities
extensive loss of feeling in fingers and toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early onset foot deformities (pes cavus and hammer toes)

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes
Distal lower limb pain and paresthesias
searchTerms: pain and numbness in lower legs
muscle cramps in hands and feet
balance issues due to sensory loss

laboratory: Normal routine blood counts and metabolic panel
imaging: Muscle MRI showing distal muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
Spinal MRI may show scoliosis-related changes
other: Nerve biopsy showing axonal degeneration with mitochondrial abnormalities
Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with slowed nerve conduction velocities
Onset usually later in childhood or adolescence
Recurrent focal neuropathies triggered by minor trauma
Lower motor neuron signs without sensory loss

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness leading to respiratory failure
Early onset severe distal muscle wasting with sensory loss
Family history of similar neuropathy with confirmed MFN2 mutation
references: Züchner S, et al. MFN2 mutations cause severe early-onset axonal neuropathy. Nat Genet. 2004.
Verhoeven K, et al. MFN2 mutations in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A. Ann Neurol. 2006.
Orphanet: Severe early-onset axonal neuropathy due to MFN2 deficiency. ORPHA:90118.
